bug_semantics: A low-privileged workflow author can supply a pathological regular-expression pattern to a Filter or Switch rule. The affected implementations parse that pattern with new RegExp() and synchronously run match()/test() once per processed item on the JavaScript worker thread, with neither complexity validation nor an execution deadline; catastrophic backtracking can therefore monopolize the worker and delay unrelated workflow executions.
flaw_origin: Commit 70728a00b7ae54c17fdd32b056f3c0dadae62947 added the Switch node and, in packages/nodes-base/nodes/Switch.node.ts, first exposed the advisory's affected-node mechanism: a user-controlled rule value was compiled at line 474 and synchronously matched against item data at line 481. Later edits extended flags/negative operations, commit 2febc61ec94928eb196e1b5f815fffa13f8bae07 copied the implementation into versioned Switch V1/V2 files, and commit 3d530522f828dfc985ae98e4bb551aa3a2bd44c6 added the analogous Filter implementation, but none is a smaller or earlier origin for the affected Switch path.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names human author and committer Jan Oberhauser <jan.oberhauser@gmail.com>, contains only the subject ':sparkles: Add Switch-Node', has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and has no bot identity.

reasoning: The advisory attack path begins when a privileged-enough workflow user configures a regex condition and a worker processes items through Filter or Switch. The historical Switch rule implementation compiles that user value and executes it synchronously for each item, so a catastrophic-backtracking pattern blocks the same worker thread. Current-path -L history must cross the 2023 V1/V2 copy/split; continuing on the predecessor file proves that the affected Switch mechanism originated in 70728a00b7ae54c17fdd32b056f3c0dadae62947, while its direct parent has no Switch source file at all. The later Filter addition is another exposure of the already-existing mechanism, not the smallest case BIC. The BIC predates all affected release boundaries, vulnerable calls remain at each immediately pre-patch tag, and branch-specific fixes first appear at 1.123.69, 2.33.4, and 2.34.1. The merged/direct fix replaces the unbounded calls with a VM-backed 250 ms timeout. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so later bot-authored bundling or fix activity cannot attribute the introduction to AI.
